promptText: Which hotel brands are commonly considered for mixed-use hotel developments in Latin America?

payload.rawResponseText:
For mixed-use developments in Latin America—typically combining a hotel with residences, offices, retail, entertainment or convention space—the following hotel groups and brands are commonly evaluated.

### Luxury and branded-residential projects

| Hotel group | Brands frequently considered |
|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W Hotels, JW Marriott, The Luxury Collection, EDITION |
| **Hilton** | Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, LXR Hotels & Resorts |
| **Hyatt** | Park Hyatt, Grand Hyatt, Andaz, Thompson Hotels |
| **IHG Hotels & Resorts** | InterContinental, Regent, Kimpton, Hotel Indigo |
| **Accor** | Raffles, Fairmont, Sofitel, SLS, SO/, Mondrian |
| **Meliá** | Gran Meliá, ME by Meliá, Paradisus |

These flags are particularly relevant when condominium or branded-residence sales help finance the development. Marriott and Accor have dedicated mixed-use and residential platforms, while IHG’s Kimpton Monterrey project illustrates the hotel-plus-residences model in Mexico. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/hotel-development?utm_source=openai))

### Upper-upscale urban mixed use

Common choices for projects incorporating offices, upscale retail, convention facilities or premium apartments include:

- **Marriott Hotels, Westin, Renaissance and Sheraton**
- **Hilton Hotels & Resorts, Curio Collection and Canopy**
- **Hyatt Regency, Hyatt Centric and Grand Hyatt**
- **InterContinental, Crowne Plaza, voco and Hotel Indigo**
- **Pullman, Swissôtel, Mövenpick, MGallery and Novotel**
- **NH Collection and Tivoli**
- **Meliá and INNSiDE by Meliá**

Hyatt Regency and Grand Hyatt have appeared in major Latin American mixed-use developments, including projects integrating residences, offices and retail. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/2012-05-21-HYATT-ANNOUNCES-COMPLETION-OF-ACQUISITION-AND-REBRANDING-OF-HOTEL-NIKKO-MEXICO-TO-HYATT-REGENCY-MEXICO-CITY-AND-ANNOUNCES-EIGHT-HOTELS-IN-LATIN-AMERICA?utm_source=openai))

### Upscale and select-service projects

For office parks, shopping centers, airports, medical districts and suburban commercial developments, developers often shortlist:

- **Courtyard by Marriott, AC Hotels, Aloft and Four Points**
- **Hilton Garden Inn, DoubleTree, Hampton and Tru**
- **Hyatt Place and Hyatt House**
- **Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Express and avid**
- **Novotel, Mercure, ibis and ibis Styles**
- **Wyndham, La Quinta, Ramada and Wyndham Garden**
- **City Express by Marriott**
- **NH Hotels and Avani**

The most consistently active select-service flags in the regional development pipeline have included **ibis, Hilton Garden Inn, Hampton, Courtyard and Holiday Inn Express**. ([lodgingeconometrics.com](https://lodgingeconometrics.com/projects-in-the-early-planning-stage-of-latin-americas-hotel-construction-pipeline-rise-at-q2-2023/?utm_source=openai))

### Extended-stay and serviced-apartment components

Where the project includes corporate housing or long-stay inventory, the usual candidates include:

- **Residence Inn, Element and Apartments by Marriott Bonvoy**
- **Home2 Suites and Embassy Suites by Hilton**
- **Hyatt House**
- **Staybridge Suites**
- **Adagio and Novotel Living**
- **Oaks Hotels, Resorts & Suites**
- **Fiesta Inn Loft**, particularly in Mexico

Extended-stay brands can work especially well beside offices, hospitals and business parks because they provide a different demand base while sharing parking, back-of-house facilities and amenities with the conventional hotel. Marriott, Accor and Hilton are actively expanding these formats. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands?utm_source=openai))

### Regional brands and operators

Depending on the country, developers may also evaluate:

- **Posadas:** Live Aqua, Grand Fiesta Americana, Fiesta Americana, Fiesta Inn, Gamma and one—especially in Mexico
- **GHL Hotels:** particularly in Colombia, the Andean region and Central America
- **Minor Hotels:** NH Collection, NH Hotels, Tivoli, Avani and nhow
- **Meliá Hotels International:** especially for resort and lifestyle developments
- Strong independent hotels using a **soft collection**, such as Autograph Collection, Luxury Collection, Curio Collection, Tapestry Collection, MGallery or Vignette Collection

Posadas has particular domestic strength in Mexico, while GHL operates across multiple Andean and Central American markets. ([posadas.com](https://www.posadas.com/en/web/posadas/nuestras-marcas?utm_source=openai))

### Practical first-round shortlist

For an initial brand-selection exercise, a typical shortlist might be:

- **Luxury hotel plus residences:** Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, Park Hyatt, Kimpton, Fairmont or SLS  
- **Premium urban tower:** Marriott, Westin, Hilton, Hyatt Regency, InterContinental, Pullman or NH Collection  
- **Lifestyle mixed use:** W, Canopy, Andaz, Thompson, Hotel Indigo, Mondrian, MGallery or INNSiDE  
- **Office/retail complex:** Courtyard, Hilton Garden Inn, Hyatt Place, Holiday Inn, Novotel or Fiesta Inn  
- **Cost-efficient commercial development:** Hampton, Holiday Inn Express, ibis, City Express, Tru or one  

Marriott, Hilton, IHG, Accor and Hyatt collectively represent the dominant group of international companies in Latin America’s hotel-development pipeline, making them the usual starting point for competitive operator solicitations. ([lodgingeconometrics.com](https://lodgingeconometrics.com/projects-in-the-early-planning-stage-of-latin-americas-hotel-construction-pipeline-rise-at-q2-2023/?utm_source=openai))

The appropriate flag ultimately depends on the city, hotel-room count, residential pricing, demand generators, available brand territory, capital cost and whether the developer wants a management agreement, franchise or third-party operator structure.
